migrations.description: Initial paykit schema: payment_transactions, ledger_entries, balance_projections (multi-wallet PK), webhook_events, reconciliation_runs
V1.5 — Add internal_id UUID column for cross-provider ID mapping (ZaloPay app_trans_id format vs paykit UUID)
V1.5 — pending_refunds table for ZaloPay 2-step refund (PROCESSING state); reconciler polls until completed/failed/timed_out
V2 — paykit.customers table; (tenant_id, provider) PK; provider_customer_id length-bounded (RT 15i)
V2 — paykit.subscriptions cache; status TEXT (RT F3); UNIQUE(provider,provider_subscription_id) (RT F10); last_event_created (RT F9)
V2 — paykit.subscription_events append-only via trigger + REVOKE on paykit_app role (RT 15j)
V2 — paykit.idempotency_records tenant-scoped Idempotency-Key replay store with 24h TTL (RT F6)
V2 — paykit.runtime_config key-value toggles with TTL; first user webhook_strict_v2 canary auto-flip (Val S4 Q3)

V2 — ledger_entries.provider + .source_id + UNIQUE (provider, source_id, entry_type) for Stripe-resend dedup (RT F1); extend entry_type CHECK with subscription_credit/refund_debit/dispute_debit/credit_note_debit
v0.2.1 hotfix — extend payment_transactions.status enum with 'quarantine' for V3 amount_mismatch path (Val Session 1 D3)
V3 Phase 03 — extend payment_transactions.status enum with 'refund_pending_webhook' for NowPayments / BitPay async refund UX (Val Session 2 D8)
V4 — merchants + api_keys tables for API-key authentication; merchant_id is root tenant entity
Scope idempotency_key unique constraint to (tenant_id, idempotency_key); fixes cross-tenant lookup isolation
V4.0 — add api_keys.created_by (nullable TEXT) for mint attribution; records acting principal (CLI operator or jwt-plane admin)
Add idempotency_records.state (in_flight|done) + nullable response_status so concurrent requests sharing a key serialize: first INSERT wins, racer gets 409 instead of double-running the handler
paykit.discounts — tenant-scoped promo codes (percent, redemption cap, expiry) for the public checkout API; race-safe consume guards the redemption cap

Add discounts.reserved so the cap counts completed payments: checkout reserves, payment webhook commits (times_redeemed++) or releases on failure; reserved+times_redeemed bounds in-flight checkouts under the cap

Add payment_transactions.provider_payment_id — captured from the webhook on credit so async-refund providers (NowPayments) can call their refund API with the provider-native payment id, distinct from provider_ref (which keys the webhook lookup on order_id)

Money columns NUMERIC(20,6) -> NUMERIC(30,0): micros have always meant whole integers, so the storage now says so and a fractional write is rejected by the database instead of silently truncated by whichever reader gets there first. Fails loudly if any pre-existing row already holds fractional micros rather than rounding it
Money CHECK constraints: payment and refund reservation amounts strictly positive, ledger entry amounts nonzero, ISO-4217 alpha-3 shape on every currency_code column that keys a wallet

The screening_pending payment status and paykit.screening_jobs — the durable handoff that keeps the tenant-supplied compliance screening call outside the crediting transaction, so a slow third-party endpoint no longer holds a payment row lock and a pooled connection for the length of its HTTP request

The paykit.refunds aggregate and the partially_refunded payment status — a refund gains its own identity and lifecycle so the ledger can be keyed per refund instead of per payment (which made every partial refund after the first collide with the first and skip its balance delta), and so a payment refunded in part is no longer recorded as refunded in full

reconciliation_runs.status gains 'partial' and 'skipped'. Both were previously recorded as 'failed', which conflated three different outcomes: a run where some providers reconciled and others errored, a run that never started because another instance held the lock, and a run where nothing reconciled at all. On a multi-instance deployment that made healthy lock contention look like a stream of failures

claim_token and claim_generation on paykit.idempotency_records — the ownership proof a finalize needs, so a claimant whose handler outlived the in-flight TTL cannot write its response into the claim a later request now holds, nor delete that claim on rollback

The provider_creating and awaiting_payment payment statuses plus checkout_result_json — a checkout attempt becomes durable before the provider is called, and the provider's answer is kept whole so a retry with the same Idempotency-Key replays the response the caller can actually use instead of a partial one

The webhook_inbox table — a received delivery becomes durable in its own transaction and its state says whether the business work committed, so a webhook that arrives before the checkout stored its provider reference becomes retryable work instead of a silent 200 that can never be redelivered
